How to Measure Yourself

Accurate measurements are the difference between a piece that fits and one that just about does. A few minutes with a tape measure now saves a back-and-forth exchange later.

What you'll need: a flexible tape measure, a mirror, and — if you can — a second person to help. Measure over light clothing, or just your underwear — not bulky layers.

Note: how tight or snug the tape sits is the real difference between a fitted and a free/loose fit — pay attention to this everywhere it matters, not just at the neck and chest.

01

The 8 Key Measurements

These cover almost everything we sell — shirts, trousers, footwear, and fitted native wear.

01Neck

Wrap the tape around the base of your neck, where a collar would sit. How much slack you leave depends on the occasion:

  • Formal, requires a tie: no slack at all around the collar.
  • Smart casual, closed collar, no tie: one finger’s width of slack.
  • Traditional — buba, senator, or any loose-fit top: one to two fingers’ width of slack.
02Chest

Measure around the fullest part of your chest, under the arms and across the shoulder blades, tape level all the way round. The same slack rule as Neck applies — none for formal, one finger for smart casual, one to two fingers for traditional or any loose fit.

03Waist

Measure around your natural waistline with no slack at all — the tape should feel exactly like a trouser sitting tight around your waist without a belt holding it up.

04Hips

Measure around the fullest part of your hips and seat, keeping the tape parallel to the floor.

05Shoulder Width

Measure across your back from the edge of one shoulder to the edge of the other, where a seam would naturally fall.

06Sleeve Length

With your arm slightly bent, measure from the shoulder edge, down the outside of the arm, to just past the wrist bone.

07Inseam

Measure from the top of your inner thigh straight down to where you want the trouser to end at your ankle.

08Shoe Size

Your regular, comfortable shoe is your true size. Measure that shoe’s length in inches or centimetres — a universal measurement — then convert it to whichever country’s sizing system you need for an accurate fit.

02

03

Traditional Wear Sizing

Agbada, kaftan, and senator pieces don't always follow the same sizing logic as Western wear — fit is often about drape and proportion as much as exact measurement.

Our recommendation: for agbada, kaftan, senator, or any fusion piece, give us your height alongside the 8 measurements above. A Wardrobe & Style Consultation or a Traditional Wear Consultation (Coming Soon) is the more reliable route for these pieces than self-measuring alone.

04

Still Not Sure?

If any of this feels like guesswork, that's completely normal — most people haven't measured themselves properly before. Home Fitting (via Personal Shopping's In-Person Fitting) or a Wardrobe & Style Consultation will get you accurate numbers with a real person doing the measuring.
